description: Add history of appendectomy at age 22
presentation: Patient is a 44-year old man who had a positive quantiferon as part of a routine medical examination given he is from an endemic country. He has no symptoms and no known TB exposures. His past surgical history is notable for an appendectomy at age 22. His chest-xray was negative for infection during his clinic visit today. He would like to delay TB treatment if not absolutely necessary for at least a few months. Does this patient need immediate TB treatment and if so, with what regimen?
